run.what: thread count and CPU affinity lever sweep
run.not_a_serving_report: llama-bench measures the engine directly, with no HTTP path. These numbers are NOT comparable to sweep.py/serving-report.schema.json figures and no report was written to benchmarks/reports/. Engine-level tg128 at t=4 was 25.36 t/s against 24.8 tok/s end-to-end through llama-server, so the serving path costs ~2%.

model.note: llama-bench reports 4.63 B params / 3.10 GiB — E2B's TOTAL params, not the 2B effective.

coverage.note: 18 cells = 9 configs x {pp512, tg128}. Nothing skipped.

findings.thread_count_is_a_weak_lever: Decode spans 22.97-25.58 t/s across t=4/8/12/16, non-monotonic, best cell 0.9% over the t=4 default and inside the error bars. Decode is memory-bandwidth bound; more cores add no bandwidth.
findings.placement_is_the_real_lever: Prefill spans 86.61-139.77 t/s, a 1.61x swing, decided by WHICH cores run it rather than how many threads.
findings.e_cores_are_stragglers: 4 P-cores alone prefill at 135.52; adding all 8 E-cores DROPS it to 116.77 (-13.8%). llama.cpp splits work evenly, so every barrier waits on the slowest thread. E-cores alone: 86.61 pp / 19.17 tg, i.e. 64% and 76% of the P-cores.
findings.smt_is_not_the_prefill_mechanism: Clean control, same 4 physical P-cores: 8 threads (0xFF) 139.77 pp vs 4 threads (0x55) 135.52 pp — +3.1% with overlapping error bars. SMT is neutral-to-good for prefill. It does cost decode 5.6% (23.49 vs 24.89), error bars just clear.
findings.confounded_cell_retained: t4-2P-smt-paired (0x0F) puts 4 threads on 2 physical cores: half the P-core compute AND SMT doubling, confounded. Its 73.50 pp is about what halving the cores alone predicts (131.86/1.8), so it is evidence about core count, not SMT. Kept because t8-P-smt-doubled was added as the clean control; do not cite 0x0F for SMT.

config_implications.THREADS: 4 — keep. Within noise of the best decode cell, and SMT costs decode 5.6%.
config_implications.THREADS_BATCH: 8 — keep, and the tpu.env rationale is CORRECT: pinned to the P-core logical threads it is the fastest prefill cell (139.77). Unpinned it measures 131.86 because threads leak onto E-cores.
config_implications.affinity: UNSET AND UNTESTED END-TO-END. The 1.61x prefill swing is reachable only by pinning, which tpu.env has no key for and server.py never passes. llama-server supports the exact split: -C 0x55 --cpu-strict 1 (decode) and -Cb 0xFF --cpu-strict-batch 1 (prefill). Engine-level only so far.
